name: crypto_metadata
description: Read the encryption metadata of a volume through the program that reads it, and say what that metadata does and does not show. Takes a file (an image of a disk or a partition) and a BYTE offset, names the scheme from the signatures at that offset (the same ones crypto_id reads: LUKS1 and LUKS2, BitLocker and BitLocker To Go, Apple Core Storage, an APFS container; the logic is copied, not imported), and runs the reader for it in the tool's own process group with a budget: `cryptsetup luksDump --dump-json-metadata` (LUKS2) or `cryptsetup luksDump` (LUKS1) on a copy of the volume's first bytes that the tool makes under its output directory and removes, `bdeinfo -o <offset>` (BitLocker), `fvdeinfo -o <offset>` (Core Storage), `fsapfsinfo -o <offset>` (APFS). The answer carries the validated scheme and its basis; the fixed fields this tool read from the bytes itself (`structural`: the LUKS header fields and, for LUKS1, the eight-slot table; the BitLocker boot sector's three metadata block offsets, each checked for the FVE signature; the APFS container's block size, the number of volume slots in use and whether the container's software-crypto flag is set); the reader's `program`, `argv`, `version` and `exit_code`; and one record per LUKS key slot (type, key size, area, KDF type and cost parameters without the salt, AF), segment, digest (the hash algorithm and which slots and segments it covers: never the salt or the digest) and token (the type only), per BitLocker key protector (its type: recovery password, TPM, clear key and the rest of libbde's list), or per count the Core Storage and APFS readers print. The first `limit` records are inline and every record is in the JSON Lines file the answer names (`all_results`), so a forged key slot count is paged, not cut. METADATA ONLY: no key, salt, digest of a verifier, UUID, label, volume or protector identifier, description or key file text is printed (the answer says each is present or not), and stderr of a reader is reported by its presence and length only. A reader's output is read through a whitelist of its labels; a line not on it is counted, not shown, and what an installed build prints for Core Storage and APFS is not established here (only its `number of ...` counts and its encryption method or state lines are shown). A reader that is not installed answers `unavailable` and is named, with the structural fields this tool read: it is never an empty list of key slots or protectors. A reader that exits non-zero (an older cryptsetup that does not know --dump-json-metadata says so in `rejected_option`), times out, writes more than 8 MiB, prints JSON or fields this tool cannot read, or disagrees with the header (a slot table, a protector count, the JSON area size) answers `partial`, with `inconsistencies` named; `complete` means the scheme was named, the reader ran to completion and its output was read to the end, not that the volume can be opened. A forged LUKS2 header size (not a power of two from 16 KiB to 4 MiB), a cut-short header and a LUKS version other than 1 and 2 answer `partial` and no reader is run on them. A signature is a lead for a reader, not a finding about the data: no match is not 'not encrypted'. Core Storage is read by fvdeinfo only, and whether the installed build reads an APFS volume is not established; fsapfsinfo's documented limits apply (no snapshots, no Fusion, no T2 encryption). The offset is in bytes (mmls works in sectors) and must be inside the file; the file is opened without following a link and without waiting (a symbolic link, a pipe, a device or a directory is refused as JSON), what is read is bounded (the first 8 KiB, at most 32 MiB copied for cryptsetup into a file `.cm-slice-*` (mode 0600) under the job's output, which the tool removes when it ends or is stopped by SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP and which a SIGKILL leaves for the caller to remove, at most 8 MiB of a reader's output), and no file the tool or a reader writes can grow past 256 MiB. Its own clock (`max_seconds`, 60 by default, at most 100) is below the manifest's timeout; it stops on SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP with one JSON answer and exit 128 + the signal, ending the reader first; a read that has not returned after the clock and a grace period ends it with one partial answer (exit 0). Withholding is by shape, measured on random draws per shape planted in a member name or path (rates, not guarantees). Printed whole in 0 of 1,000 draws: hexadecimal ids of 16, 32 and 64, numbers of 10 digits or more, recovery passwords written with dashes, spaces, dots, underscores, no separator or one to three of any other characters between the groups (an en dash, a comma, a colon, a pipe, a tab), also when the groups are cut at the separators of the path (123456-123456/123456-...), full-width, split by invisible characters, or with one decimal digit glued to the first or last group, AWS access key ids, password= and api_key: assignments, user-info, 4x4 groups of capitals and digits joined by - or ., letters and digits of 8, 9, 12, 16 or 40 characters that hold a capital, a small letter and a digit, and a full-width id. Printed whole in some draws: uniform draws of letters and digits (every character as likely a capital, a small letter or a digit as any other) of 8 characters about 2.5%, of 9 about 2%, of 12 about 1%, of 16 about 0.6%, of 24 at most 0.1% and of 40 none; random lowercase letters and digits of 8 about 7%, of 12 about 2.4%, of 16 about 0.4%; 24 random letters 1.5% to 2.6%; a 16-character base32 id 2.2% to 3.4% (by alphabet); four groups of four lowercase hexadecimal digits joined by underscores 4% to 9% (by how the draws are made); an id of 12 or 16 characters whose letters are half Cyrillic or Greek look-alikes about 1%. NOT recognised, by design, and printed whole: an identifier of 7 characters or fewer, a number of 9 digits or fewer, a lowercase-only run of up to 22 letters (it reads as a word), an all-capital letters-only run of any length, three groups of four or five capitals and digits joined by - or . (a rule for them would also withhold upper-case constants such as OpenSSL manual page names), a recovery password cut by anything other than a separator or with a letter in it or glued to it (the groups then show), a ten-digit number written 3-3-4, an e-mail-like lowercase string, and a secret of any other shape; a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. What the rule is given is bounded: a string of more than 4096 characters (as written or after folding), a path of more than 8192, or a string with a / and a run of more than 256 name characters is withheld whole as '<text too long to judge withheld>' and not judged (the slowest string inside the bound that a search found took 0.13 CPU s). The output check, which reads every printed string once more, is narrower than the rule: with the rule removed it replaces recovery passwords (full-width ones too), AWS ids, password= values, PEM headers, user-info, hexadecimal of 16 digits or more and runs of 24 or more characters that flip between letters and digits, and it lets through numbers of 10 to 20 digits, ids of up to 23 characters, some base64 (about one in five of 32 bytes), every recovery password whose groups are joined by anything but a hyphen, underscore, dot, space or nothing, and every recovery password cut over the components of a path (the first layer alone holds those). The rule also changes names that are not secrets: of the file names of a documents tree 6.9% have a part withheld (10-digit timestamps, UUIDs) and 0.6% of its directories, of an application tree 16% and 3.1% (a word with a digit inside, such as libmp3lame, is withheld in part). A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 2: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape. The reader's output is read from files this tool redirects it to: a process the reader (or its version probe) leaves behind is ended before they are read; every answer that is not a refusal or an error carries `program_group` (subreaper, left_behind, unproven, notes), and a `complete` answer is `partial` when a process was ended and when the host cannot rule one out (not Linux, or the kernel refuses PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER).

path.description: A volume image (a file made from a disk or a partition); a symbolic link, device node, pipe or socket is refused

offset.description: Byte offset of the volume within the image (bytes, not sectors; default 0). It must be inside the file

limit.description: Records returned inline (default 100, 1 to 1000); every record is in the file all_results names

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 60, 1 to 100; the manifest's timeout is 120)
